findings.title: Preserve range-variable detection before interpolation
findings.body: This interpolates the expression before `querySupportsSplitting` checks `isQueryWithRangeVariable`. When Grafana resolves `$__range`, the guard no longer sees the variable and a query that is explicitly meant to avoid splitting is partitioned into time chunks. The chunks then use an interpolated range value rather than the original backend-per-request range behavior, changing query semantics and potentially repeating full-range scans. Determine split eligibility from the original expression, or retain its range-variable status through interpolation.

findings.title: Avoid applying template variables twice to sharded targets
findings.body: The shard path interpolates targets here, then passes each shard request to `runSplitQuery`, which now calls `applyTemplateVariables` again. Template interpolation is not generally idempotent: if a variable's value contains a literal `$name` sequence, the second pass can interpret it as another variable and silently change the query sent to Loki. Apply variables once in this path, or ensure the nested split call does not re-interpolate already-expanded targets.
